name: MT-Bench-101
abstract: MT-Bench-101 evaluates fine-grained instruction following in multi-turn dialogue. This page uses the Avg score from the paper.
contributions: The benchmark emphasizes fine-grained multi-turn capability decomposition rather than a coarse chat score.
The page preserves the paper's original 10-point scale.
method: MT-Bench-101 is designed for fine-grained evaluation of multi-turn dialogue, addressing the fact that prior dialogue benchmarks are often too coarse or too focused on single-turn settings.
By analyzing real multi-turn conversations, the paper builds a three-level ability taxonomy spanning 13 tasks, 1,388 dialogues, and 4,208 turns.
This allows the authors to compare models not only on overall dialogue quality but also on how their abilities change across turns within different tasks.
The study finds that common alignment techniques and chat-oriented designs do not clearly improve multi-turn ability, leaving real conversational interaction as a major challenge for LLMs.
leaderboard_note: The leaderboard directly uses the paper's Avg. Because the benchmark itself is already a fine-grained decomposition, this page does not recombine additional columns.
